about: the path and confounder claims of Knowledge in cdnod, xges, hc, tabu, mmhc, rsmax2, grasp, exact_search, iamb, inter_iamb, mmpc, fci_jci, grasp_fci, and multi_group_direct_lingam: on simulated data, each method with true claims against the same fit without them, and against reference packages given the same knowledge. The rows of pc, ges, boss, fci, gfci, boss_fci, lpcmci, and direct_lingam, and the exactness lanes, are in published/0.16.0/knowledge-paths.json. The fits with path claims of cdnod, iamb, inter_iamb, and mmpc ran at the build that applies claims to the undirected edges of a graph with no consistent extension; no_consistent_extension describes the rule, compares those fits with the fits before it, and holds pc's rows under it.
build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 on the 0.17.0 release branch (commit 7faf5d667, version string 0.16.0); the fits with path claims of cdnod, iamb, inter_iamb, and mmpc, and pc's under no_consistent_extension, at commit 307292bad of the same branch

lanes.cpdag: xges, hc, tabu, mmhc, rsmax2, grasp, exact_search, iamb, inter_iamb, mmpc (iamb, inter_iamb, and mmpc with structure=cpdag and no target): linear-Gaussian, Erdos-Renyi, standardized; d 10, 20, 50; n 500, 2000; expected degree 2 and 4; claims on 5, 10, 30% of the ordered pairs. exact_search runs the four cells at d 10 and the two at d 20 with expected degree 2.
lanes.cdnod: cdnod: 4 domains whose means shift, linear-Gaussian, Erdos-Renyi; d 10, 20, 50; n 500, 2000; expected degree 2 and 4; claims on 5, 10, 30% of the ordered pairs
lanes.jci: fci_jci: two domains and one context variable, hidden confounders, linear-Gaussian, the simulation of Mooij et al. (2020); 10 and 20 system variables; 500 and 2000 rows per domain; claims on 10, 30% of the ordered pairs and of the confounded pairs
lanes.pag: grasp_fci: linear-Gaussian, Erdos-Renyi, standardized, with hidden nodes; 10 observed and 2 hidden, 20 and 3; n 1000, 5000; claims on 10, 30% of the ordered observed pairs and of the confounded pairs
lanes.multigroup: multi_group_direct_lingam: 3 groups that share one DAG, linear, uniform noise; d 10, 20, 50; n 500, 2000 per group; claims on 10, 30% of the ordered pairs; errors are summed over the 3 groups' graphs

verdict_rule: per method, cell, part, and fraction: D = errors(with true claims) - errors(without) per dataset, seeds 0-19; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies above 0, better when below; a worse row counts only when the same row on seeds 100-119 is worse too in the same measure. The cpdag lane judges two measures, errors and dag_errors (dag_* fields), and a row worse again in either counts. cdnod is judged by dag_errors, its distance to the true DAG; its errors, the distance to the class the domain index identifies, are reported. Floor: the interval of errors - empty-graph errors must lie below 0. A row with in_setting false lies outside the method's stated setting (hc, tabu, and xges at expected degree 4) and is reported, not judged. A part of a method passes when no judged row is worse again, every judged row is below the floor, and every dataset was fit. The exactness lanes of published/0.16.0 cover these methods through the step they share: restrict_paths for the 11 that return a CPDAG, the PAG rule for fci_jci and grasp_fci, and the order rule of direct_lingam for multi_group_direct_lingam.
error_metric: jci, pag, multigroup: pairs adjacent in the fit and not in the truth, or the reverse, plus every tail or arrowhead, on a pair adjacent in both, that differs from the true MAG of the observed variables (jci, pag) or the true DAG (multigroup, summed over the groups); a circle is never wrong. cpdag, cdnod: errors is the structural Hamming distance (andrey.metrics.shd) to the class the truth and the fit's true claims define, the true CPDAG without claims (in cdnod, the CPDAG the domain index identifies) and the MPDAG of the true class under the claims with them; dag_errors is the endpoint-aware distance to the true DAG (an edge directed as the DAG directs it 0, an undirected edge 1, a reversed, missing, or extra edge 2); reversed_with and reversed_without are the mean numbers of edges directed against the true DAG; edges_directed_by_claims counts, on pairs adjacent in the truth, the edges directed with the claims beyond those directed without, and of_them_against_the_true_dag those directed against the true DAG
dropped_note: claims is the number of true claims given to the fits of a row and dropped the number the fits dropped as unmet by the graph they found; knowledge_error counts fits that raised. For cdnod, iamb, inter_iamb, and mmpc, applied_to_an_edge is the number of claims that directed an undirected edge of a graph with no consistent extension, and no_consistent_extension counts the fits with such a graph and their claims
no_dataset_note: seeds whose graph has too few nodes with two children to hide the cell's hidden nodes; left out of the pag lane

no_consistent_extension.about: pc, cdnod, iamb, inter_iamb, and mmpc direct edges by tests and can return a graph with no consistent extension, one that stands for no DAG. Before this rule a fit dropped every path claim on such a graph. Under it a claim on a pair joined by an undirected edge directs that edge (a -> b for a required path from a to b, b -> a for a forbidden one) and Meek's rules follow; a claim the pair's directed edge already meets changes nothing; a claim on a pair that is not adjacent, a claim against a directed edge, and claims that conflict (both directions of one edge, or a directed cycle) are dropped. A fit without path claims, and a fit whose graph has a consistent extension, are unchanged.
no_consistent_extension.build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 on the 0.17.0 release branch (commit 307292bad, version string 0.16.0); the fits before the rule ran at commit 7faf5d667 (cdnod, iamb, inter_iamb, mmpc) and are pc's rows of published/0.16.0
no_consistent_extension.what_was_refit: the fits with path claims (arms true and false) of the five methods on every cell and fraction, seeds 0-19, each paired with the recorded fit of its dataset without claims; the fits without claims and with edges hold no path claim and were not refit (the build returns the recorded scores on each of the 1,200 fits without claims and on a sample of the fits with edges)
no_consistent_extension.new_against_old_rule: per method, cell, part, and fraction: D = errors(fit under the rule) - errors(fit before it) per dataset, both with the same true claims, seeds 0-19; the interval, verdict, and measures as in verdict_rule
no_consistent_extension.new_against_old_rows: no_extension_rows, at the end of the file: one row per method, cell, part, and fraction, with the mean number of claims applied to an edge (edge_claims) and dropped (unmet_new, unmet_old) per fit
no_consistent_extension.fresh_seeds: the five rows worse than without claims on seeds 0-19 (errors; pc required_paths d10-n2000-deg2 5%, pc forbidden_paths d50-n500-deg2 5%, iamb and inter_iamb forbidden_paths d50-n500-deg2 5%, mmpc forbidden_paths d50-n2000-deg2 30%) were fit again on seeds 100-119 with the fits without claims of the same build; each row's replicate field holds the result, and none was worse again. No row was worse than the fits before the rule, so none of that comparison was fit again.
no_consistent_extension.before_note: the same rows before the rule: each method with true claims against the same fit without them (rows by verdict, D, edges directed) and the number of claims its fits dropped
no_consistent_extension.claims_note: per method and part in verdicts and pc_from_0_17_0: claims, dropped, and claims_applied_to_an_edge over all fits with true claims; no_consistent_extension counts the fits whose graph has no consistent extension and, in them, the claims applied to an undirected edge, met by a directed edge, and dropped
no_consistent_extension.pooled_rule: beyond the two-group rule: the three cpdag cells fit again on seeds 100-119 (d10-n2000-deg2, d50-n2000-deg2, d50-n500-deg2) with both seed groups pooled, 40 datasets a row; D = errors(with true claims) - errors(without), the same bootstrap. A part with a row worse here is not promoted, though no row is worse on both groups separately.

pc_from_0_17_0.about: pc with true path claims under the rule, from 0.17.0; published/0.16.0/knowledge-paths.json holds pc's rows before it and is unchanged. The same_edges comparison holds no path claim and equals 0.16.0's.

false_claims_note: rows with arm false state 10% of the ordered pairs wrongly: context, not judged

references.about: each method against a reference package given the same knowledge, on the datasets of the lanes above; seeds 0-19, worse rows of the like-for-like comparison repeated on seeds 100-119

packages.bnlearn.tabu: bnlearn 5.2.1 tabu, score bic-g, whitelist and blacklist

packages.bnlearn.rsmax2: bnlearn 5.2.1 rsmax2 with restrict mmpc and maximize hc, Fisher z at alpha 0.05 and score bic-g, whitelist and blacklist
packages.bnlearn.iamb: bnlearn 5.2.1 iamb, Fisher z at alpha 0.05, whitelist and blacklist; its partially directed graph read as the CPDAG
packages.bnlearn.inter_iamb: bnlearn 5.2.1 inter.iamb, Fisher z at alpha 0.05, whitelist and blacklist
packages.causal_learn.cdnod: causal-learn 0.1.4.8 CD-NOD, Fisher z at alpha 0.05, required and forbidden edges as background_knowledge

references.translation: the references of the cpdag, cdnod, and pag lanes take edges, not paths: a forbidden path a -> b becomes the forbidden edge a -> b; a required path on a pair adjacent in the true graph becomes the required edge a -> b; a required path on any other pair, and a confounded pair, has no edge form and is left out. A required edge says more than the path it comes from: it states that the pair is adjacent.
references.arms: same_edges: the method with the translated edges as required and forbidden against the reference with the same edges. same_claims: the method with the claims against a reference that takes the claims themselves (lingam). claims_against_reference: the method with the path claims against the reference with the translated edges; not like for like, reported on seeds 0-19, and repeated on fresh seeds only where a cell was rerun for another row. without_knowledge: both without knowledge. hc_bic and tabu_bic are hc and tabu with ebic_gamma=0, the plain BIC of bnlearn's bic-g.
references.rule: per method, reference, cell, part, and fraction: D = errors(method) - errors(reference) per dataset both fit, dag_errors in cpdag and cdnod and errors elsewhere; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D (10,000 resamples) lies above 0; a worse row counts when the same row on seeds 100-119 is worse too. Rows with in_setting false (hc and tabu at expected degree 4) are reported and not judged. A part of a method is supported when it passes the checks above and, with the same knowledge as the reference (same_edges or same_claims), no judged row of its own, or of the all-parts runs for required_paths, is worse again against a reference; a method with its default settings must also be below the floor in those rows. Where no reference takes the knowledge (no_reference), the comparison with the same fit without the claims is the whole check, as for confounded in 0.16.0. The floor is judged with the method's default settings: hc and tabu with ebic_gamma=0 are not below the empty graph at d50-n500-deg2 with or without claims, as bnlearn is not, and status lists those rows under plain_bic_floor, not as a reason.
